evidence.title: The Provo shoreline of Lake Bonneville
evidence.excerpt: G.K. Gilbert studied the Bonneville basin 150 years ago and his findings have largely stood the test of time: The Provo shoreline, the most prominent geomorphic feature of Lake Bonneville, reflects threshold-stabilized overflow of the lake after the Bonneville flood and before a drier climate caused the lake to shrink. Subsequent refinements in chronology allow the Provo lake to be identified as about 18.2–14.8 cal ka BP, and stratigraphic studies show that the lake was gradually growing deeper during that time. evidence.excerpt: The Provo shoreline of Lake Bonneville formed following the Bonneville flood, and, based on previous dating, was formed during a period of overflow from about 17.5 to 15.0 cal. ka. source_ledger.title: What Lake Bonneville Left Behind - NASA Science
source_ledger.excerpt: Image of the Day for August 24, 2026. At its peak, ancient Lake Bonneville would have been a sight to behold. Nearly as large as Lake Michigan, the Ice Age lake spread across much of western Utah and parts of Nevada and Idaho. Lake Bonneville began forming about 55,000 years ago. Then, about 18,000 years ago, water breached that dam, unleashing a torrent that entered the Columbia River system. Over a six-week period, amid one of North America's largest floods, lake levels plummeted by more than 350 feet (105 meters). Remnants include today's Great Salt Lake, Utah Lake, and Sevier Lake. In this image captured by the OLI on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite, bathtub-like rings and wave-cut terraces trace the position of former shorelines. In June 2026 NASA scientists working with the DAVINCI mission came to Crater Island to field-test cameras. In August 2026, Andy Green set a record for the fastest land speed in a hydrogen-fueled internal-combustion vehicle, reaching 406.320 miles per hour. Story by Adam Voiland.

what_happened.text: NASA Earth Observatory published an August 24, 2026 Image of the Day, “What Lake Bonneville Left Behind,” using Landsat 8 OLI imagery of former shorelines, playas, and salt flats in the Bonneville basin, with a story by Adam Voiland.

why_it_matters_now.text: The same leftover lakebed is framed as current news: a June 2026 DAVINCI camera rehearsal at Crater Island and an August 2026 hydrogen land-speed mark sit inside a brand-new NASA image package, not only Ice Age geology.

verified_facts.text: The page is NASA Earth Observatory’s Image of the Day for August 24, 2026, titled “What Lake Bonneville Left Behind,” with images by Michala Garrison from USGS Landsat data and a story by Adam Voiland.
The article says Ice Age Lake Bonneville was nearly as large as Lake Michigan and spread across much of western Utah and parts of Nevada and Idaho.
It states the lake began forming about 55,000 years ago after volcanic eruptions in what’s now southeastern Idaho diverted the Bear River, with a natural dam at Red Rock Pass.
It states that about 18,000 years ago the dam breached into the Columbia River system and, over six weeks, lake level fell more than 350 feet (105 meters).
It names today’s Great Salt Lake, Utah Lake, and Sevier Lake as remnants after later warming and drying.
The featured Landsat 8 OLI image is described as showing bathtub-like rings and wave-cut terraces of former shorelines, with a pale dried lakebed of clay, marl, and sandy sediment.
It describes evaporite salt flats (halite, gypsum, and potassium- and magnesium-bearing salts) and rectangular potash evaporation ponds.
It reports June 2026 DAVINCI camera tests at Crater Island, nicknamed “Venus on Earth,” and an August 2026 Andy Green hydrogen-fueled run of 406.320 mph on the salt flats.

tension_or_argument.text: Keep the satellite geology (rings, terraces, pale sediments, evaporites, named ranges) separate from the article’s human overlay—engineering feats, Donner-Reed desperation, speed records, and a Venus analog. The photo does not itself prove the flood chronology or those stories.

surprising_details.text: The article calls the Red Rock Pass outburst one of North America’s largest floods and says the drop took about six weeks.
DAVINCI rehearsals hung the camera system from a helicopter; the team says image-only 3-D maps matched existing geologic maps, intended as practice for Venus’s Alpha Regio.
Mickey Thompson’s 1960 406.60 mph mark and Green’s 2026 406.320 mph hydrogen mark sit within a mile-per-hour of each other on the same flats.
In August 1846 the Donner-Reed Party, heading from Hastings Pass past Floating Island toward Donner Spring, broke through thin salt crust into mud and abandoned wagons.

flexible_outline.text: Open on the August 24, 2026 NASA Image of the Day: what Landsat 8 actually shows—bathtub rings, wave-cut terraces, pale playa vs. darker mountains.

Walk the article’s lake history only as stated: ~55,000-year start, Bear River diversion, Red Rock Pass dam, ~18,000-year six-week flood, leftover Great Salt Lake / Utah Lake / Sevier Lake. Flag that this packet does not include the primary papers.
Name the leftover materials the piece specifies: clay/marl/sand lakebed, evaporite crusts, potash ponds, and the Silver Island, Newfoundland, and Pilot ranges plus Crater Island rocks.
June 2026 DAVINCI “Venus on Earth” camera drop at Crater Island and why NASA ties those rocks to Alpha Regio mapping.
Bonneville as a speed surface: Thompson 1960 vs. Green’s August 2026 hydrogen internal-combustion mark, staying inside the article’s numbers.
Donner-Reed August 1846 wagons mired south of Crater Island—color only, not proof of the shoreline science.
